newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SIA sees Asian-US open skies pact.
newsitem.headline: SIA sees Asian-US open skies pact.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong said on Tuesday he expected an open skies agreement between Asia and the United States.
"There will be open skies, and they will come sooner rather than later," Cheong said in a speech on the National Aviation Press Club of Australia.

Cheong said he was confident of an open skies agreement between the United States and some Asian countries, despite no accord reached following talks recently between U.S. and avation authorities in South Korea, Taiwan, Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei.

Cheong said Singapore and Malaysia were willing to agree on an open skies agreement with the United States, but the U.S. wanted the agreement of a critical mass of Asian countries before it signed any agreement with any Asian nation.

He said he was disappointed with the U.S. stance, as the U.S. started its open skies policy with Europe by first agreeing with the Netherlands on an open-skies pact before it signed agreements with 10 other European nations.
Britain, which is one of the few major European nations not to have an open-skies agreement with the U.S., is to resume trans Atlantic air services talks with the U.S. this week.

"The United Kingdom is holding out, but depending on how talks on the proposed British Airways -American Airlines alliance unravel, it too may find open-skies with the U.S. irresistable," Cheong said.
Progress in the long-running talks is crucial to whether the U.S. authorities approve British Airways proposed alliance with American Airlines.

Australia should also consider an open-skies pact with the U.S. and that Singapore would support such a move, said Cheong, who is visiting Australia following talks with the Australian government on bilateral aviation issues.

"It would be in Australia's interests to do the same, not only because of the economic benefits that would flow from this, but also because it would be in line with the stated desire of Australian political leaders to move closer economically and politically towards Asia," Cheong said.
Cheong said talks with the Australian government last week did not result in any agreement, but more meetings would be held in a few months time.
Cheong would not comment on the content of the talks.
